title: Same-looking curves, different physics
status: SILENT ROUGH CUT · NORMALIZED MODELS · NOT APPROVED
projection_notes: Depth lost: h = x cos α + y sin α; vertical = z
intro_labels: Field line → follows a vector field
sources: NASA CCMC · Properties of Magnetic Dipoles
Original visuals · no RH, NS or common-physics claim
dipole_labels: Normalized, not a real magnet interior

cues.heading: What does each curve represent?
cues.caption: Similar-looking curves can describe different mathematical objects. Start with their definitions.

cues.heading: Start with points on x = 1
cues.caption: Take a line in the input plane. Apply the point map w = z².

cues.heading: Map points — not a force
cues.caption: Matching dots show z = 1 + iy and w = (1 − y²) + i(2y).

cues.heading: Return to the original x,y plane
cues.caption: Now choose V = Re(z²) = x² − y² as a local potential. That is a modelling choice.

cues.heading: Contour ≠ field line
cues.caption: Dashed contours keep V constant. Solid field lines follow E = −grad V, crossing regular contours normally.

cues.heading: New model: a 3D magnetic dipole
cues.caption: These ideal field lines follow B in three dimensions, outside the excluded source. This is a different model.

cues.heading: Cut to a view looking along y
cues.caption: The same two fixed 3D curves have different depths. In this x,z view, their outlines overlap.

cues.heading: Turn only the camera
cues.caption: The orthographic camera turns by 30°. All physical points and the magnetic field stay fixed.

cues.heading: Different view — unchanged field
cues.caption: Their projections separate. The dashed curve is edge-on; the underlying curve has not collapsed.

cues.heading: Check the definition before the shape
cues.caption: Which object has a tangent parallel to its vector field: mapped grid, potential contour, or field line?

cues.heading: Field line: tangent parallel to the field
cues.caption: The answer is field line. Definitions and equations establish the connection; visual resemblance alone does not.
